mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month averages signals a robust demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 4% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, but also consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a low-inflation environment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for six consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE < 4% for six months and inflation is low.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five consecutive months of INDPRO above its 12-month moving average.
